name: container-app
description: Azure Container Apps running a container image with HTTP autoscaling. Dev scales to zero; prod keeps a warm, zone-redundant baseline.
what: Azure Container Apps running any container image behind external HTTPS ingress, with HTTP concurrency autoscaling, a managed identity, and logs streamed to Log Analytics. Dev scales to zero; prod runs a warm, zone-redundant baseline.
why: When you already have a containerized app, Container Apps gives you serverless scale (including scale-to-zero) and revision-based rollouts without operating Kubernetes. You pay per second of actual usage, which suits spiky or intermittent workloads.
potentialUseCases: Microservices or event-driven workers that scale with load
A containerized API or background processor with bursty traffic
Cost-sensitive dev/test apps that should idle at near-zero cost
Migrating a Docker Compose app to managed, autoscaling hosting

reliability: Warm baseline replicas in prod avoid cold-start failures
Managed environment handles rolling revisions and health probes
security: System-assigned managed identity for downstream access
No secrets in the image - use Container Apps secrets / Key Vault
costOptimization: Scale-to-zero in dev (minReplicas 0) - pay only when serving traffic
Right-size cpu/memory per replica to the workload
operationalExcellence: Container logs streamed to Log Analytics
performanceEfficiency: Scales out to maxReplicas under load

quota.summary: Needs Container Apps managed-environment (vCPU/memory) quota in the target region. New regions or constrained subscriptions can hit per-region Container Apps quota at preflight.

requirements.detail: The managed environment needs available vCPU/memory quota for the requested replica sizing in the region.
